name: Window Controls Overlay and Tabbed mode
plain: Lets an installed app draw into the title bar, or show tabs.
meaning: Customises the app window chrome on desktop.

access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

data.metric: Lets an installed app draw into the title bar, or show tabs.

limits.headline: Can draw into the title bar of an installed app, like showing tabs or search
limits.user_action: You install the web app on a computer and open it
can: Place buttons or a search box in the title bar of the app window
Keep the system's close and minimize buttons
cannot: Work for a site that is not installed
Hide the close, minimize or maximize buttons
Work in Firefox, Safari or on phones
See anything outside its own window
limits.differs: Chrome and Edge on computers only. Phones, Safari and Firefox do not support it.

story.what_it_is: An installed desktop web app can draw its own design in the title bar, or show tabs there.

marketing.name: Window Controls Overlay
marketing.pitch: Lets installed web apps use the full window, including the title bar area, so they look like desktop apps.

story.for_you: The app uses the whole window, with its search bar or tabs in the top strip. It looks more like a real desktop program. Window buttons still work as usual.
story.for_makers: Makers get a premium look and more space for tools. It helps web apps match desktop apps for design. It is used for polish, and only works for installed apps on desktop.

use_cases.example: A web design app puts its toolbar in the title bar, which gives the canvas more space.
A chat app puts its search box in the title bar, like a native chat app.
A web music player shows now playing in the top strip.
A web code editor shows tabs in the title bar to save room.
A web game launcher uses the full window with its logo in the title bar.
A web video editor shows the project name and tools in the top strip.
A company dashboard app shows alerts in the title bar.
